items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The script (4763 bytes) is not shown. It reproduces the reference MOG/foot-tracking algorithm the agent read in solve.sh, which uses cryptic positional indexing such as data[np.argmax(data[:, 2])] and jump[8]/jump[7]. The log has no evidence these were renamed.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The algorithm was ported from the reference, which does measurement and jump selection in one extraction function with nested filtering and repeated max/min logic. Debug artifacts (/app/debug_frames, test_video.mp4) were removed at step [90]. Structure is standard but partly monolithic.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Thresholds are absolute pixel constants copied from the reference: crop_height=15, foot_width=5, video_width=960. The log shows no cap.isOpened() check. Error handling is probably a generic ValueError on 'no movement data'.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: The normal path works on both videos (54/63 and 222/232). Detection depends on fixed pixel constants (15, 5, 960), not adaptive thresholds. Validating input opening and handling no detection are not shown to exit non-zero with a clear message.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads argv[1] (step [84] used test_video.mp4) and falls back to the example video. Writes /app/output.toml with exactly jump_takeoff_frame_number = 54 and jump_land_frame_number = 63 as integers, with no extra velocity key.
